supersedes: nothing; extends protocol 1.0 (configs/protocol.json), whose results are frozen in results/v1_freeze/MANIFEST_v1.sha256
title: Physiology-Aligned Multiresolution Analysis for Patient-Independent Heart-Murmur Detection: A Comparative Study of Wavelet and Fourier Features
research_question: Does cardiac-cycle timing alignment improve patient-independent murmur detection, and does the wavelet-vs-Fourier choice matter once alignment is controlled?
unchanged_from_v1: binary Present vs Absent, Unknown excluded
WPD depth 4, db4 primary, order=freq, periodization

representations.wpd: WPD db4 raw squared coefficients (v1 primary)
representations.wpds: WPD db4 energies smoothed along time with the STFT's 64-sample Hann (4-tap over level-4 columns) -- now pre-registered

conditions.perm: PRIMARY NULL: column labels randomly permuted within each recording (np.random.default_rng(crc32(rec_id)).permutation); same counts of S1/systole/S2/diastole/unannotated, timing destroyed; same 34-feature definitions
conditions.shift: SECONDARY NULL: label sequence circularly shifted by u*T columns, u ~ U(0.2,0.8) from the same seeded RNG, T = median S1-to-S1 interval of that recording (0.6 s if <2 S1 events); caveat: shifts near 0.5T can partly invert systole/diastole

hypotheses.H5d_secondary: RF AUROC(true) - AUROC(shift) >= 0.03 for each representation

E2_isolate_alignment.rule: SUPPORTED iff delta >= 0.03 AND subject-bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0 AND delta > 0 in >= 18/25 outer folds; otherwise NOT SUPPORTED
E2_isolate_alignment.interpretation_if_not_supported: the v1 aligned-pipeline gain is attributed to feature definitions/normalisation, not to physiological timing

E1_automatic_segmentation.segmenter: unsupervised, uses no murmur labels and no expert .tsv: (1) homomorphic envelope of the 25-400 Hz band (|Hilbert| -> log -> 8 Hz low-pass -> exp, 50 Hz rate); (2) heart period T = envelope autocorrelation peak in [0.3, 1.5] s; (3) heart-sound peaks = envelope local maxima with min spacing 0.2*T and height >= 25th percentile of envelope; (4) consecutive peak intervals paired, shorter interval of each pair = systole (S1 -> S2), longer = diastole (S2 -> S1); (5) S1/S2 extents = contiguous region around the peak where envelope >= 50% of the peak value, clipped to [40, 160] ms; (6) everything else labelled 0 only if no valid pairing exists
E1_automatic_segmentation.parameter_freeze: all constants above are fixed now; no tuning on classification results. Any change must be justified by segmentation metrics only (no murmur labels) and logged as an amendment before rerunning classification
E1_automatic_segmentation.segmentation_evaluation: against expert .tsv inside expert-annotated spans: S1 and S2 centre detection F1 with +/-50 ms tolerance; frame-wise 4-state accuracy

hypotheses.H6b: RF AUROC(auto, wpd) > AUROC(B1) with subject-bootstrap CI lower bound > 0
hypotheses.H6c: same as H6a/H6b for stft and wpds (reported, same rule)

E1_automatic_segmentation.flag: if S1/S2 F1 < 0.70 the downstream result is still reported, flagged as 'low-quality segmentation'

E3_soft_murmurs.status: DROPPED 2026-10-27 22:35 IST (not run): time, and E1 showed segmentation is the bottleneck
E3_soft_murmurs.feature: per recording: log(mean systolic energy in 62.5-187.5 Hz / mean S1 energy in 62.5-187.5 Hz) using wpd and stft maps, added to the aligned set
E3_soft_murmurs.hypothesis: H7: sensitivity on grade I/VI Present patients at the spec80 operating point increases by >= 0.05 with overall RF AUROC not below the v1 value minus 0.01

equivalence_report: for wpds vs stft (aligned, true labels): report delta and 95% CI; say 'no meaningful difference' only if the whole CI lies within +/-0.03
forbidden: as v1; additionally: no re-selection of segmenter constants, null definitions, or representations after seeing E1/E2 classification results

E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.preregistered: 2026-10-27 22:35 IST, designed AFTER the E1 results were known (E1 S1/S2 F1 0.510/0.493, all H6 NOT SUPPORTED); E1 unchanged
E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.source: Springer, Tarassenko & Clifford, IEEE TBME 63(4):822-832, 2016; MATLAB reference PhysioNet hss v1.0 (DOI 10.13026/vnt9-kf93, GPL-3.0); Python port in src/ec418/segmentation/lr_hsmm.py (GPL-3.0). Not used: EchoStatements/Springer-Segmentation-Python (no licence), pyPCG-toolbox 0.1b5 (no training)
E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.fixed_from_paper: 1 kHz audio; Butterworth order-2 LP 400 Hz + HP 25 Hz zero-phase; Schmidt spike removal; 50 Hz features z-scored per recording: homomorphic envelope (order-1 8 Hz LP), Hilbert envelope, 40-60 Hz PSD (25-sample Hamming, 13 overlap, 1 Hz bins), |rbio3.9 level-3 detail| (repeated 2^3, central part); per-state unpenalised logistic regression vs equal-size random other-state sample; emission P(s|o) N(o;mu,Sigma)/0.25; cyclic transitions; Gaussian durations truncated at mean +/- 3 SD (systole +/- 3(SD_sys+SD_S1)), normalised over 1..D, D=round(T*50); Springer extended duration Viterbi; HR/systolic interval from autocorrelation of 1 kHz homomorphic envelope. resample_poly for features; PSD to envelope length by linear interpolation
E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.learned_from_training_annotations: S1/S2 duration mean and SD (rounded to 50 Hz samples, SD>=1); systole SD = pooled within-recording SD; diastole SD = a*mean+b by OLS of within-recording SD on mean (>=1 sample); mean_systole = systolic interval - mean_S1; mean_diastole = T - systolic interval - mean_S2; period search range = [p1, p99] of per-recording median S1-S1 onset interval; systolic search range = [p1, p99] of per-recording median(S1->S2 onset)/median(S1->S1 onset) times T. Training samples = 50 Hz samples inside valid expert rows (labels 1-4)
E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.leakage_control: per outer fold (r,k): test patients decoded by a segmenter trained on all training patients of (r,k); training patients decoded by cross-fitting over the 3 frozen inner folds; Unknown-murmur recordings (not classified) decoded by a segmenter trained on all 874 binary-task patients (segmentation report only); seeds 1000r+10k+i (i=0 outer, 1-3 inner), Unknown model 9999
E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.segmentation_report: as E1 (S1/S2 centre F1 +/-50 ms, 4-state frame accuracy, failures, by Present/Absent/Unknown and v1.0.3 age) on test-fold decodings; primary repeat 0; low-quality flag if S1 or S2 F1 < 0.70
E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.classification: 34 aligned features for stft, wpd, wpds (same extractor); WEKA RF primary, SMO secondary; frozen folds; tag e1b; fold-specific feature files

hypotheses.H8b: RF AUROC(auto-HSMM, wpd) > AUROC(B1) with subject-bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0
hypotheses.H8c: H8a and H8b for stft and wpds

E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.statistics: as E1: repeat-averaged scores, 2000 subject resamples seed 2, both AUROC summaries, fold counts reported; descriptive vs W_stft, vs E1 auto sets, grade sensitivity
E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.runtime_rule: time on ~50 recordings; if the full 25-fold estimate exceeds ~4 h, commit an amendment reducing to repeat 0 only (5 folds) BEFORE running, with repeat-0 comparators
E1b_lr_hsmm_segmentation.timebox: if classification is not complete by 2026-10-30 23:59 IST, stop and report as incomplete

E4_span_selector.preregistered: 2026-10-27 23:30 IST, designed AFTER diagnostics D1-D3 were known; tag e4-prereg; no E4 code before it
E4_span_selector.windows: non-overlapping 1-s windows from t=0 (125 level-4 columns, 50 HSMM samples, 4000 raw samples); trailing partial window dropped (never selected, not used for training/evaluation)
E4_span_selector.target: window annotated iff >= 50% of its columns have expert label 1-4 (column_labels of the expert .tsv); no murmur labels or patient metadata
features: log10 P(20-200 Hz)/P(0-1000 Hz), Hann power spectrum of the raw 4 kHz window, eps 1e-12
log10 P(25-400 Hz)/P(0-2000 Hz), same spectrum

highest local max of the normalised autocorrelation of the E1 homomorphic envelope (v1-preprocessed 2 kHz signal) at lags 0.3-1.5 s on a 3-s context centred on the window (shifted inside the recording; whole recording if shorter); 0 if none
Fisher kurtosis of the raw signal band-passed 500-1000 Hz (Butterworth order 4 zero-phase, whole recording) within the window
clipping fraction: share of raw int16 samples with |x| >= 32767

mean over the window's 50 Hz samples of max over states of the LR-HSMM per-state logistic-regression P(state|o) (no forward-backward in the port: LR state probability, not an HSMM posterior), from the patient's E1b HSMM model
E4_span_selector.model: StandardScaler on the detector's training windows + L2 LogisticRegression C=1.0 (lbfgs, max_iter=1000)
E4_span_selector.threshold: probability quantile on the detector's own training windows at which the predicted annotated fraction equals that set's expert annotated fraction
E4_span_selector.cross_fitting: test patients: detector trained on all training patients of (r,k); training patients in inner fold i: detector trained on the other training patients; HSMM labels and feature 6 use the E1b per-patient HSMM assignment (re-decoded, checked identical)
E4_span_selector.classification: E1b HSMM labels kept only in predicted-annotated windows; same 34 aligned features stft/wpd/wpds, coverage minimum, aggregation; WEKA RF primary, SMO secondary; frozen folds; tag e4
E4_span_selector.report: detector window AUROC/accuracy and predicted vs expert annotated fraction on test-fold windows (primary repeat 0), by Present/Absent and age; missing features by class; classification both AUROC summaries
